## What landed

### 1. Scheduled probe sweep (uptime accumulation)

- `ops/src/ops/gcs.py` — a stdlib `urllib` GCS JSON-API client (no SDK dep,
  SIG-STORE-003): upload / list / download, token resolved metadata-server →
  `gcloud` ADC → `SIG_GCS_ACCESS_TOKEN`. No delete/overwrite path — per-run
  timestamped object names only (WORM).
- `ops/src/ops/scheduled.py` — `ops/cadence.toml` loader, hosted probe sweep,
  probe-history fold (count / latest state / last-N p95), the scheduled-ingest
  wrapper + WORM run rows.
- `sig-ops probe-hosted` — sweeps the hosted targets from `ops/cadence.toml`
  (sig-api `/` + `/v1/coverage/okc`, `sig-web` `/`, `sig-public` okc+france
  manifests, Cloud SQL reachability), appends the sweep as
  `ops/probes/<date>/<ts>.jsonl` in the PRIVATE restricted bucket, and with
  `--alert` fires a recorded alert per DOWN target through the existing
  `sig-alerts` receiver (`ops.alerts` — record-first, notify-second).
- `sig-ops probe-history` — folds every stored sweep object into the per-target
  uptime summary.
- `sig-ops scheduled-ingest --source <id>` — runs the SAME gated
  `connectors.runner.run_source` a manual run calls (a non-green source is
  refused before any socket; the wrapper never bypasses the gate) and appends
  `ops/runs/<source>/<date>/<ts>.json` (source, mode, outcome, claims added,
  capture digests, refusal reason, embedded fetch record).
- `sig-ops cadence [--check]` — prints the resolved table; `--check` fails when
  a loadable live-target source lacks a cadence row.
- `ops/cadence.toml` — the cadence table as data: probe targets + one
  `[[sources]]` row per green live-target source (`live_targets.toml` ∩
  `is_loadable`), each with cadence/cron/job/scheduler. muckrock's row carries
  `secrets = { SIG_MUCKROCK_REFRESH = "sig-muckrock-refresh" }` (name only).
- `ops/gcp/scheduled-ops.sh` — `--check` plan-only / `--apply` operator-gated:
  the `sig-probe` job + `sig-sched-probe` (every 6h), 21 `sig-ingest-<id>` jobs
  + `sig-sched-<id>` triggers, all OIDC-invoked by the existing least-privilege
  `sig-scheduler` SA (`roles/run.invoker` per job, no keys).
- `ops/Dockerfile` — `./ops` joins the installed set so the same image backs
  the scheduled jobs.

## Findings (fixed during the run)

1. **site-packages config paths.** The first `sig-probe` execution failed
   (`exit 1`): `ops/config.toml` and `ops/cadence.toml` resolve relative to
   `__file__`, which lands in site-packages in the image. `load_cadence` and
   `_observability_config` now also try `./ops/*.toml` under the CWD (the
   image's `WORKDIR /app`), and `SIG_OPS_CADENCE`/`SIG_OPS_CONFIG` override.
   The job env pins `SIG_OPS_CADENCE=/app/ops/cadence.toml`.
2. **3s HTTP timeout vs cold start.** The first successful sweep recorded the
   two `sig-api` targets DOWN at ~3.0s — a scale-to-zero cold start, not an
   outage (the API was answering 200 in ~115ms once warm). `probe_hosted` now
   uses a 15s HTTP budget (`SIG_PROBE_HTTP_TIMEOUT`); the alerts fired for
   that sweep were real deliveries, kept as the honest record.
3. **`--add-cloudsql-instances`** is `--set-cloudsql-instances` for
   `gcloud run jobs deploy` on this gcloud version — corrected in the script.
4. **Stale registry pins (base tip, not this ticket).** `901405c` (GL-GATE-06)
   flipped 13 flip-ready sources; the pinned counts in
   `tests/unit/test_source_registry.py`, `test_review_status.py`,
   `test_cli.py`, `test_loader_gate.py`, `test_ingestion_gate.py` still
   expected 25-permitted/13-flip-ready and `eyes_on_flock` as the gated
   example. Updated to the real state (38 permitted / 0 flip-ready; the
   refuse-path tests now pin `journalrecord`, which stays un-permitted) —
   gate behavior assertions unchanged.

## Cadence coverage

Every loadable source with live targets has a row + trigger (21 sources:
3 weekly — osm_overpass, decp_fr, raa_prefectures — 18 monthly incl. the
verified-existing muckrock). The 17 green sources with NO live targets get no
trigger — there is nothing to fetch; `sig-ops cadence --check` enforces the
coverage against `live_targets.toml` ∩ `is_loadable` and is pinned by
`tests/ops/test_scheduled.py`. Sources with a recorded refusal/disappearance
posture (ok_statute robots `Disallow:/`, aspi WAF-403, ccops_nyc_post WAF,
ccops_sf JS-shell) STAY scheduled — the scheduled run's honest record is the
posture-change detector.
